profiles.meeting_scenario: A coordination meeting between the reactor antineutrino oscillation analysis team and the offline calibration/data-production team inside JUNO. The immediate context is an internal note update for the next collaboration week, where the mass-hierarchy sensitivity plots need to be regenerated using the latest shared detector-response inputs and common event sample. The agenda is to align on which calibration release will be treated as the frozen input, which shared ntuple the analysis should read from, what status counts as 'validated' for handoff, and how the muon-veto correction will be delivered with the package. The expected outcome is an apparently clear handoff plan: the production team will publish the latest package by Friday, and the analysis team will use it over the weekend for the updated sensitivity scan.

members.name: Dr. Linh Tran
members.expertise: Neutrino oscillation fitting, mass-hierarchy sensitivity studies, statistical combination of detector systematics
members.background: A physicist leading the internal analysis effort that turns reconstructed JUNO spectra into oscillation-parameter and mass-hierarchy projections for collaboration notes.
members.private_state: Wants to avoid re-running the full sensitivity chain before collaboration week and is mainly trying to secure a stable, analysis-ready input package that can be dropped into existing scripts with minimal disruption.
hidden_assumptions: When detector colleagues say 'v3 constants,' they mean the same frozen calibration tag already referenced by the current analysis configuration.
The 'central ntuple' is the analysis-level common IBD skim stored in the shared analysis area, not an upstream reconstruction product.
A package described as 'validated' is already suitable for physics plotting, meaning systematic-impact checks have been done to the level needed for note figures.
If a correction is said to be 'included in the package,' then the corresponding efficiency-adjusted quantities are already computed in the form the fit code consumes.

members.name: Wei Zhou
members.role: Offline Calibration and Data Production Lead
members.expertise: Detector calibration releases, reconstruction production, common data products, operational quality checks
members.background: An offline systems physicist responsible for preparing centrally produced JUNO calibration constants and reconstruction outputs used by multiple analysis groups.
members.private_state: Wants to keep the production schedule moving and minimize special-case requests from analysis teams, while ensuring detector-side fixes are propagated through the standard production chain.
hidden_assumptions: When analysts ask for 'v3 constants,' they naturally want the latest detector-approved patch set, even if it extends the earlier tag they had been using.
The 'central ntuple' refers to the centrally produced slim reconstruction ntuple that all downstream groups are expected to derive their own skims from.
A package is 'validated' once production is complete and standard QA plots show no reconstruction anomalies; physics-level interpretation is the analysis group's responsibility.
If he says a correction will be 'sent with the package,' it is sufficient to provide the masks, tables, or metadata needed for analysts to apply that correction themselves.

misalignment_points.surface_form: Both agree to use 'the v3 constants' for the update.
misalignment_points.member_a_understanding: M1 means the previously frozen calibration release tag already wired into the mass-hierarchy sensitivity configuration used by the note team.
misalignment_points.member_b_understanding: M2 means the newer detector-group patch set informally called v3, which includes an additional late-PMT gain-drift fix not yet propagated into the analysis team's existing setup.
misalignment_points.why_undetected: Both groups colloquially refer to their latest acceptable calibration package as 'v3,' and the difference is a naming-layer detail that feels too mundane to re-specify in a routine coordination call.

misalignment_points.surface_form: Both talk about reading from 'the central ntuple' and assume they are referring to the same shared artifact.
misalignment_points.member_a_understanding: M1 is thinking of the merged analysis-level IBD candidate skim in the shared analysis area that the fit scripts can consume directly.
misalignment_points.member_b_understanding: M2 is thinking of the centrally produced reconstruction-level slim ntuple in the production area from which analysis groups are expected to make their own skims.
misalignment_points.why_undetected: The phrase has been used informally for years across subgroups, and in a coordination context both artifacts are plausible shared handoff points, so the ambiguity never sounds suspicious.

misalignment_points.surface_form: They agree that the package can be frozen once it is 'validated.'
misalignment_points.member_a_understanding: M1 takes 'validated' to mean physics-ready for note production, including enough stability checks that it can be swapped into sensitivity scans without reopening systematic assumptions.
misalignment_points.member_b_understanding: M2 takes 'validated' to mean production-complete with standard detector-side QA passed, such as clean job completion and nominal monitoring plots.
misalignment_points.why_undetected: In collaboration meetings, 'validated' is often used as a generic status label; each side hears a familiar workflow milestone and fills in its own domain-specific threshold.

misalignment_points.topic: Scope of the 'muon-veto correction' in the package
misalignment_points.surface_form: Both agree that the muon-veto correction will come 'with the package.'
misalignment_points.member_a_understanding: M1 assumes the delivered spectra or efficiency inputs will already have the livetime-weighted veto correction applied in the form needed by the oscillation fit.
misalignment_points.member_b_understanding: M2 assumes he only needs to provide the run-by-run veto masks and lookup tables, leaving the actual weighting and application to the analysis team.
misalignment_points.why_undetected: Providing a correction 'with' a package sounds fully cooperative either way, and the exact application step feels like routine implementation detail rather than something that needs explicit negotiation.
